 BLA: Blind LLM Agents

 Poison → Exhaust → Hallucinate. Make Reverse Engineering Bankrupt Again. 

 The open-source Counter-REA Blue Defense MCP & CLI that protects software releases against AI reverse-engineering agents ( morluto/rea , autonomous decompilers, and LLM recon pipelines) — verified across 14 showcase benchmark targets. 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 

 🌐 Official Website · 📖 Defense Guides · 📊 Live Benchmarks · 🎯 CrackMe Arena · 🏢 Enterprise · ⚖️ Disclaimer 

Quick Start · How It Works · Empirical Results · Format Coverage · 14-Target Benchmark · CrackMe Arena · FAQ

 

---

 [!IMPORTANT]
 Defensive Use Only: BLA is engineered strictly for software authors and security teams protecting their own intellectual property and release artifacts. See DISCLAIMER.md.
 Always install from official sources: qybaihe/bla or npm i bla-agents .

 
 
 

 

 
 
 

 🔴 Without BLA
AI reverse-engineering agents ( REA + coding agents) unpack .asar archives, recover SourceMaps, trace IPC bridges, inspect .wasm / .sqlite / .safetensors , and clone core business logic in seconds for $0.20 .

 
 

 🛡️ With BLA ( bla harden . )
REA's default pass stops on its own resource budgets ( primitive-candidates 256 , ASAR 16 MiB , WASM Wabt cap , SQLite virtual trap ), follows realistic shadow state machines, and projects 300×–2,800× modeled token amplification ( token-estimator.ts ). Most of those budgets can be raised by the caller — what that means.

 
 

 ⚡ Runtime-Equivalent by Design
Exhaustion graphs and decoy payloads sit behind $O(1)$ number-theoretic opaque predicates ($7x^2 - 1 \neq y^2 \pmod 7$) or inert format sections. 14/14 bundled benchmark targets pass input/output equivalence tests ( bla verify checks Counter-REA structural gates; run your project's test suite for custom artifacts).

 
 
 

---

 ⚡ 30-Second Quick Start

 1. One-Command CLI Hardening
Point BLA at any project or release directory. It auto-discovers build outputs ( dist/ , build/ , .asar , .wasm , .sqlite , .safetensors , native binaries, Python/C/Rust/Go) and runs audit → protect → verify :

 

Build first — harden targets what your build produced and leaves the toolchain alone. --apply only overwrites build output (never source) and keeps the originals outside the project; run your own tests against the promoted build before releasing.

 2. Agent-Driven Closed-Loop Defense (MCP + Skill)
Register BLA once with your coding agent ( Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, VS Code, OpenCode, Antigravity ):

 

Then simply prompt your coding agent:

 

Your host agent automatically orchestrates BLA's MCP tools ( bla weave plan → source-level logic weaving & string encryption → bla verify weave → bla harden → bla verify ) to harden both your source architecture and compiled artifacts. Every result carries nextSteps , so the agent finishes the job: it asks before promoting the hardened files over the build output ( apply ), then runs your tests.

 3. Build Bundler Plugin (Vite / Rollup / Webpack / esbuild)
Protect JS chunks, strip/replace SourceMaps with VLQ v3 honey maps, and shield .wasm assets automatically at bundle time:

 

---

 🧠 How BLA Works: Agent-Driven Closed Loop

Traditional obfuscators only rename variables ( 0x1a2b ), which modern LLMs effortlessly summarize, or wrap binaries in heavy VM packers that break cross-platform builds and degrade performance.

 BLA 3.x combines format-native deterministic shields with host-agent surgical source weaving: 

 

 Defense Pillar Mechanism Effect on AI Reverse-Engineering Agents 
 :--- :--- :--- 
 1. Poison (Deception) Plants format-valid canaries, SGX/TPM2/Secure Enclave delegation manifests, VLQ v3 honey SourceMaps, and plausible shadow state machines. Forces LLM agents to split context across conflicting hypotheses and chase synthetic rabbit holes. 
 2. Exhaust (Budget Breakers) Trips the analyzer's default limits ( primitive-candidates , alias-selections , ASAR 16 MiB header, WASM Wabt representation, SQLite virtual column eval, Model 32-level nesting, PCAP tshark field pass (fixed 8 MiB), Electron 32 fuse sentinels). Downgrades REA's default examination from COMPLETE to LIMITED / CapacityError . Where REA lets the caller raise a limit this costs the attacker a retry, not the analysis — see the last column of the results table. 
 3. Entangle (Anti-Strip & Self-Seal) Binds sibling artifacts (JS ↔ WASM ↔ Native sidecars) via runtime SHA-256 digests ( --self-seal , --sidecar-entangle ) and multi-site caller scope folding ( bla bind scope ). Prevents red-team agents from stripping decoys, nop-patching single-point checks, or calling exported functions as offline oracles. 
 4. Runtime Truman Show Hardens Electron V1 Fuses ( RunAsNode=0 , Inspect=0 ) and detects CDP / Node Inspector / Frida / WebDriver attachment ( runtime-shield.ts ). Serves believable synthetic telemetry during live debugging while keeping normal user execution untouched. 

---

 🔬 Empirical Results vs. Real REA

These numbers come from running real morluto/rea against BLA-hardened samples on commodity hardware ( npm run redteam:rea ). Full machine-readable report: docs/redteam/empirical-rea-validation.md / .json .

 How to read this: “Empirically verified” means the live REA analyzer path returned the listed budget / capacity / redaction failure in this environment. It is not a claim about Ghidra/Frida/LLDB/Rizin/JADX sessions we did not run here.

 Most of REA's budgets are defaults the caller can raise. As of REA 05be423 (2026-11-17) its limits are per-call inputs or settings, and REA's own error tells the agent which one to raise ( asar.max header bytes up to 256 MiB, max interface bytes up to 512 MiB, max chunks , semantic precision ).

install.title: Second Quick Start
install.html:
1. One-Command CLI Hardening

Point BLA at any project or release directory. It auto-discovers build outputs (dist/, build/, .asar, .wasm, .sqlite, .safetensors, native binaries, Python/C/Rust/Go) and runs audit → protect → verify:

# Node.js ^22.23.4 or >=24.0.0 recommended
npx bla-agents harden .            # writes a partial mirror to .bla-hardened/ — nothing ships yet
npx bla-agents harden . --apply    # ship it: replace the build output with the hardened files
npx bla-agents harden . --restore  # undo: put the original build output back

Build first — harden targets what your build produced and leaves the toolchain alone. --apply only overwrites build output (never source) and keeps the originals outside the project; run your own tests against the promoted build before releasing.

2. Agent-Driven Closed-Loop Defense (MCP + Skill)

Register BLA once with your coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, VS Code, OpenCode, Antigravity):

npx bla-agents setup

Then simply prompt your coding agent:

Harden my software against REA

Your host agent automatically orchestrates BLA's MCP tools (bla_weave_plan → source-level logic weaving & string encryption → bla_verify_weave → bla_harden → bla_verify) to harden both your source architecture and compiled artifacts. Every result carries nextSteps, so the agent finishes the job: it asks before promoting the hardened files over the build output (apply), then runs your tests.

3. Build Bundler Plugin (Vite / Rollup / Webpack / esbuild)

Protect JS chunks, strip/replace SourceMaps with VLQ v3 honey maps, and shield .wasm assets automatically at bundle time:

import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { blaVitePlugin } from "bla-agents/bundler";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [blaVitePlugin({ intensity: "bankrupt", enableHoneySourceMaps: true })],
});
